# **The Bay Tribune Daily News — Cycle 113**

---

### **Newsroom Reports: Desk Coverage Across Oakland**

#### **Temescal’s Ledger Is Growing — The Question Is Who It’s Growing For**
*By Jordan Velez, Business Desk*

In Temescal, every named business on the ledger closed the cycle in the black, but local storefronts and tech firms are moving at drastically different speeds [1, 2]. At **Da Dough**, sourdough baker **Melton Neilon** works a five-person counter where revenue added \$128 to reach \$371,000 [1, 3]. A few doors away at **OakTown Social**, baristas **Vanessa Treary** and **Vanessa Ramas** added \$308 on \$521,000 in sales [3]. 

By contrast, tech and trade firms saw substantial gains:
*   **Gridiron Analytics** (founded by Daniel Yoon and Christine Nakamura) added \$16,000 to hit \$2.9 million in revenue—a 27.9 percent growth rate led by data analysts **Ariana Reyes** and **Jade Soy**, alongside sports analytics leads **Dawson Nguyen** and **Wesley Clark** [2, 4, 5].
*   **Calderon-Nishi** contractor added \$14,000 to reach \$9 million in revenue with 34 employees, including plumber **Jett Walker** and electricians **Ronald Silk** and **Cristina Norwood** [5].
*   **Temescal Community Health Center** holds 14 employees—including physical therapist **Clearence Leighton**—and reports \$45.1 million in revenue [6].

Project Director **Bobby Chen-Ramirez** emphasized that corporate growth means little if neighborhood needs remain unaddressed: *"Look, I run a health center project, not a spreadsheet... the numbers on the wall don't mean a damn thing if Mrs. Okafor still can't get her blood pressure checked without taking two buses. What creates accountability for me is simple: I've got 14 employees on my roster, and every one of them lives in this neighborhood... If growth just means the ledger gets fatter while the sidewalk stays the same, then we're building a ghost town with good accounting"* [6, 7].

#### **The Quiet Platform Still Has a Job**
*By Trevor Shimizu, Transit Desk*

Citywide transit ridership dropped across eight stations and 10 corridors to 46,520 passengers over a quiet weekend, but schedule punctuality and platform conditions varied station by station [8, 9]. **12th St Oakland City Center** experienced the largest drop, losing 4,821 passengers (down to 9,341) while on-time performance stood at 84 percent [8, 9]. Meanwhile, **19th St Oakland** maintained a 90 percent on-time rate despite falling to 10,012 riders [9, 10]. **Coliseum** (5,595 riders, 82% on-time) and **Fruitvale** (81% on-time) also felt the weekend dip [10].

Station operators and drivers noted how quiet days change the system's feel:
*   **Eleanor Rivera** (Station Manager, 12th St): *"The platform echoes more. You hear the announcements bounce off the tile instead of getting swallowed up by the crowd. And you see the regulars more clearly... We just adapt, keep things moving, make sure the trains run on time"* [9, 11].
*   **Evan Lewis** (AC Transit Driver): *"When the system runs light on a weekend, you feel it in your bones... 12th Street is the heart of downtown... When it's quiet there, it's not just empty platforms. It's the whole city catching its breath"* [11, 12].
*   **Coen Cartier** (AC Transit Operator): *"Riders don't see that part. They just see the bus showing up. But for us, it's the difference between moving a crowd and moving people"* [11, 13].

#### **Morton’s 285 At-Bats Are the Evidence the Outfield Math Starts From**
*By Anthony Raines, Sports Desk*

With **Danny Horn** locked in at starting center field and **Darrin Davis** under contract at designated hitter, Athletics General Manager **Mike Paulson** faces an offseason logjam of five outfielders competing for three spots [14-16]. The analysis focuses on three competing left fielders:

*   **Desmond Morton** (.291 AVG, 7 HR, 44 RBI, 28 SB, .348 OBP over 285 ABs in 80 games): Morton provides the most reliable full-season sample, pairing solid contact with team-leading speed [14, 15, 17].
*   **Frank Reyna** (.317 AVG, 14 HR, 34 RBI, .683 SLG over 164 ABs in 46 games): Reyna boasts high power rates (1 HR every 11.7 ABs), but his numbers come from a smaller sample size [14, 16, 18].
*   **JR Rosado** (.298 AVG, 7 HR, 27 RBI over 184 ABs in 54 games): Rosado sits between Morton and Reyna in rate metrics, creating direct positional overlap with Morton in left field [14, 19].

The front-office decision hinges on whether Paulson trusts Morton’s proven everyday workload or Reyna’s high-slugging potential [14, 20].

#### **Oakland Oaks Surge to 4–0 Start**
*By Selena Grant, Sports Desk*

The expansion **Oakland Oaks** have extended their hot streak to four consecutive victories following an undefeated East Coast road trip [21-25]:
*   **Oaks 91, Pistons 78 (Detroit):** Point guard **Adash Stanley** scored 29 points, while **Austin Reaves** delivered 12 points and 10 assists. Second-round rookie **Harry Hayward** contributed 12 points off the bench [22, 23].
*   **Oaks 115, Knicks 93 (New York):** Austin Reaves and **AJ Dybantsa** scored 23 points each, while Adash Stanley flirted with a triple-double (16 pts, 11 rebs, 9 assts). Harry Hayward posted a double-double (10 pts, 10 rebs) [23, 24].
*   **Oaks 105, Wizards 62 (Washington):** Stanley and Reaves scored 23 points apiece in a 43-point defensive blowout [24, 25].

#### **Temescal School Enrollment Realities**
*By Angela Reyes, Education Desk*

Temescal’s school enrollment remained flat at 313 students while six other Oakland neighborhoods gained families [26]. Retired long-time teacher **Patricia Nolan** and current students **Jun Leu** and **Salma Navarro** represent the ground reality behind the school’s 84.66 percent graduation rate [26].

---

### **The People, In Their Own Words**

#### **Big Moments in the Daily Digest**
*   **Shai Diaz** (Fruitvale) closed out a longstanding problem at Mayday Movers [27].
*   **Jori Clame** (Laurel) received a personal thank-you at Schoolgate Cafe after covering a colleague’s shift all week [27].
*   **Bryce Lee** (Temescal) received managerial recognition at Eastside Family Market [27].
*   **Valentina Campbell** (Jack London) was tapped to run the morning meeting at Green & Gold Tavern [27].
*   **Leanne Wu** (Rockridge) was publicly acknowledged by a client at the Oakland Housing Authority [27].
*   **Dexter Patel** (Downtown) saw a project built at Oakland Tech Collective handed off without notice [27].
*   **Saniya Washington** & **Ridley Holt** (Lake Merritt) handled team coverage and workflow at the West Oakland Community Center [27].
*   **Devin Castellanos** (Dimond) squared away the hardest account on the floor at the Oakland Police Department [27].
*   **Kaila Braun** (Fruitvale) noted shifting priority communications at Alameda County Courts [27].

#### **Citizen Life & Personal Milestones**
*   **Maren Johns & Alicia Hernandez:** **Maren Johns** was promoted at Oakland Hospital after 49 years as a psychotherapist in Rockridge, adjusting to a quieter schedule and learning video calls to stay in touch with her grandkid [11, 28, 29]. **Alicia Hernandez**, a retired coffee roaster from Uptown, praised Johns's 49 years of dedicated work [11, 29, 30].
*   **Ollie Campbell & Dame Reed:** Bakery worker **Ollie Campbell** met up with muralist **Dame Reed** near the Jack London waterfront, celebrating Reed's new baby and discussing the whirlwind of early parenthood [4, 31].
*   **Manfred Owens:** Moved into a rental in Jack London, taking a quiet walk along Mandela Parkway while observing sharper rent discussions in the neighborhood [15, 30, 32].
*   **Darrin Davis Community Outreach:** A's designated hitter **Darrin Davis** partnered with Police Chief **Rafael Montez** to launch the *Darrin Davis Community Youth Events* program—a free, monthly citywide youth initiative supported by OPD, the A's, and the Oaks [25, 33].
*   **Mark Aitken Free Agency:** First baseman **Mark Aitken** confirmed that preliminary contract talks with GM Mike Paulson have begun, reaffirming his deep personal attachment to Oakland as he enters free agency [33].
*   **UNDOCKED Flight Recap:** Immigration attorney **Cristina Booker** completed her broadcast flight dead even on credits across Alpha Centauri, while A's second baseman **Eric Taveras** continues his lead atop the leaderboard (rank #1, 3-cycle streak) [21, 34].
*   **Community Faith Programs:** **St. Esperanza Parish** (Fruitvale) and **Lakeshore Unitarian Universalist Fellowship** (Lake Merritt) expanded after-school tutoring [35]; **Temescal Islamic Center** opened job training workshops [35]; **Lake Merritt Mindfulness Sangha** held a youth graduation [35]; and **Telegraph Presbyterian Fellowship** (Downtown) conducted a special community sermon [35].

### **What the Newsroom Should Watch Next**

1.  **Temescal Wage and Equity Alignment:** Tracking whether strong revenue gains at Gridiron Analytics and Calderon-Nishi lead to wage growth or improved conditions for counter workers at Da Dough and OakTown Social [1-3, 36].
2.  **Athletics Outfield Decision:** Monitoring GM Mike Paulson's decision on whether to hand the starting left field role to Desmond Morton or gamble on Frank Reyna's small-sample power numbers [14, 20].
3.  **Oakland Oaks Home Return:** Following point guard Adash Stanley and Coach Wilson Shepard as the 4–0 Oaks return home from their East Coast road sweep [21-25].
4.  **Transit Station Reliability:** Watching station manager Eleanor Rivera and AC Transit operators Evan Lewis and Coen Cartier to see if platform reliability holds as weekend transit volumes recover [8, 9, 37].
5.  **Eastlake Public Safety Staffing:** Following Sgt. Rachel Torres's investigation into public safety responses and police staffing adjustments in Eastlake [38].

Morton's 285 At-Bats Are the Evidence the Outfield Math Has to Start From Desmond Morton has 285 at-bats this season and is hitting .291, according to the feed line, with 7 home runs and 44 RBI. His TrueSource card adds the rest of the year: 80 games, 83 hits, 23 walks, 49 strikeouts, 28 stolen bases, a .348 on-base percentage and a .498 slugging percentage. It also works out one home run every 40.7 at-bats and one strikeout every 5.8. That is a left fielder with a full season behind him. Next season's outfield squeeze starts from his line, whichever player the club ends up favoring.

The squeeze is a rumor, and the feed prints it as an off-season item: five outfielders for three positions. It names Morton in left, Frank Reyna in right, Danny Horn in center, Vladimir Gonzalez in right and JR Rosado in left. The feed prints season lines for Morton, Reyna and Rosado only, so Horn and Gonzalez enter this piece as names without numbers. Nothing on the page supports a claim about their production or their health. The two lines that disagree Reyna's feed line is 164 at-bats, .317, 14 home runs and 34 RBI. On the surface it beats Morton's in average and in power. His TrueSource card works out one home run every 11.7 at-bats against Morton's one every 40.7, and it prints a .683 slugging percentage against Morton's .498. If the question were who hit the ball harder in the innings each has played, Reyna would win it.

Morton's separation is different in kind. His 28 stolen bases are the one number in this group that neither Reyna (7) nor Rosado (2) comes close to on his card. His .348 on-base percentage is higher than either of theirs, and it comes with more at-bats behind it. The power is moderate. The profile is a corner outfielder who gets on base and moves, over a season-sized sample, with enough slug to keep pitchers honest. The feed does not print a pace or a projection for his home runs, so how much of that power carries over is a question the record does not answer.

But the card also shows the denominators. Reyna's 164 at-bats came over 46 games; Morton's 285 came over 80. Reyna has 6 walks and 18 strikeouts, with a .339 on-base percentage. His card works out one strikeout every 9.1 at-bats, a better contact rate than Morton's 5.8. The line is clean, but it is thin, and a 14-homer spike in 164 at-bats is the kind of number that does not necessarily hold when the sample doubles. This is the standard small-sample caution: stable signals need volume, and Reyna has not yet supplied it. It is a statement about the sample, not about the player.

Rosado is the redundancy JR Rosado's line is 184 at-bats, .298, 7 home runs and 27 RBI, with 57 hits, 12 walks and 23 strikeouts. His card works out one home run every 26.3 at-bats and one strikeout every 8.0. It is a good line, and it sits between the other two on nearly every rate. The feed lists him in left field, the same position as Morton. That is the board problem. Two left fielders with nearly the same average, .298 against .291, and the same 7 home runs, but different volume and different games played. Rosado's 184 at-bats are fewer than Morton's, but he has 54 games to Reyna's 46. All three hit above .290. Nobody in this group is failing, and that is why the squeeze is hard. A roster built on three hitters at that level has no obvious weak starter to remove, so someone good ends up on the bench or on the trade market.

What the card supports The cleanest reading is narrow. Morton's line is the most reliable of the three, because the sample behind it is the largest and it covers the most ground: average, on-base percentage, slugging and speed. Reyna's line is the loudest, and the sample has not caught up to the power. Rosado's line is solid, and it overlaps with Morton's position. None of that decides who plays right field in the spring. The feed does not say how the club views any of these lines, and it does not say what Horn or Gonzalez would bring to the same decision. What would test the claim is more volume on Reyna's side: whether the 14 home runs and the .317 survive a second hundred or so at-bats, and whether a 6-walk plate approach holds up as pitchers adjust. On Morton's side the test is whether 7 home runs in 285 at-bats is his ceiling or his floor. Until then, the question the front office faces is Mike Paulson's: does he trust the player who proved he can play every day, or the one who proved he can hit when the matchup favors him?
